title: Implement incremental merkle tree computation using frontier

story.i_want_to: refactor AuditChain.sign_and_store_tree_head/1 to compute merkle tree incrementally: fetch only entries above the previous STH's chain_position, compute the tree for only those entries, and fold the result into the previous merkle root using the stored frontier
story.so_that: STH computation becomes O(new entries) instead of O(total history), reducing database load during peak activity when many tenants are active

rationale: The current compute_merkle_root/1 fetches all entry hashes from genesis and rebuilds the entire tree every minute. With the frontier persisted (from US-35.1), we can compute only on the delta. The frontier stores the sibling hashes needed to attach a new subtree to the root; folding is just hash(prev_root, new_subtree_root), replacing O(n) work with O(log n) work.

acceptance_criteria.description: A new function AuditChain.compute_merkle_frontier/2 (tenant_id, last_position) returns {frontier_path, merkle_root} for entries above last_position

AuditChain.compute_merkle_root/1 is unchanged in signature but internally checks for a previous STH; if one exists and frontier is present, it calls compute_merkle_frontier; if not, it falls back to the current full-recompute path
sign_and_store_tree_head/1 extracts the frontier from compute_merkle_frontier and stores it in the merkle_frontier field of the new STH
Incremental computation works correctly for tenant chains from 0 entries (genesis) to millions of entries (incremental path taken)
The merkle_frontier field is populated on every new STH insert via sign_and_store_tree_head/1
The final merkle_root computed incrementally matches the root that would have been computed by re-scanning the entire chain (deterministic correctness)

test_cases.name: compute_merkle_frontier returns correct frontier and root for delta entries
preconditions: An STH exists at position 500 with frontier
steps: Verify the returned frontier is a list of hashes
Verify the returned merkle_root is a 32-byte binary
expected_results: frontier length is O(log(chain_size)), not O(new_entries)

test_cases.name: Incremental merkle_root matches full recompute
steps: Compute merkle_root via full recompute (current path)

test_cases.name: sign_and_store_tree_head populates merkle_frontier
preconditions: A tenant exists with an existing STH
A new entry has been appended
expected_results: merkle_frontier is populated and is a binary

test_cases.name: Genesis STH (first entry) uses full recompute fallback
preconditions: A new tenant exists with no STHs
expected_results: Fallback to full recompute works (no previous STH to fold against)

notes: The frontier is a serialized list of hashes; use the same merkle_tree/1 helper but capture the intermediate hashes during recursion. Consider a helper like merkle_tree_with_frontier/1 that returns both the root and the frontier path (a list of hashes at each level of the tree). Binary encoding (e.g., frame by length or just concatenate) is fine for storage; decode it on retrieval.
